back: How a writer presents a character: description, actions, speech, thoughts and others' reactions.
Major characters drive the story and usually change; minor characters support the plot or reveal others.
Where and when a story happens, including its social world; it creates atmosphere.
Exposition → rising action → climax → falling action → resolution.
Internal: a struggle within a character's mind. External: against another person, nature or society.
A topic is a word (family); a theme is an idea about it (family loyalty can demand sacrifice).
First person uses I and is inside the story; third person uses he/she/they from outside.
Writers reveal character through actions and details rather than stating qualities directly.
notes: Taking the biggest cobs and checking who saw → greedy and sly.

front: Writing about a book you have read
back: Title and author, brief spoiler-free outline, one supported point on character or theme, personal response with reasons.
